A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SupGCL research work, with 22 pages and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of SupGCL on cancer gene regulatory networks, including downstream prediction results in Tables 2–3 and additional metrics, embedding analyses, and sensitivity results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix F, including classification, survival prediction, and embedding analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain the same biological supervision, artificial augmentations, shared GNN, loss decomposition, and Algorithm 1. The corrected summation index clarifies the existing loss formulation; it does not establish a change to the training procedure.

E1.justification: Both use TCGA patient networks and LINCS knockdown teacher networks for breast, lung, and colorectal cancer, with the same 13 downstream tasks. Dataset and population coverage in Appendix C is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain w/o-pretrain, GAE, GraphCL, GRACE, and SGRL. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced in the main or appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–E retain the same sample sizes, preprocessing, data splits, five-layer Graph Transformer, default embedding dimension, tuning settings, training budgets, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix F retain the same t-SNE visualizations, PCA analysis of latent-space collapse, and embedding-dimension sweep over 8, 16, 32, and 64 dimensions. No analysis or robustness test is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations, ten-fold evaluation, and ten random-seed undersampling runs for cancer-relevance classification. The uncertainty reporting in tables and Figure 6 is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, SupGCL breast subtype accuracy remains 0.847 ± 0.036 in Table 3, and its macro F1 remains 0.785 ± 0.056 in Table 12.

T1.justification: Equation 8 and its repetition at the start of Appendix A correct the outer summation from i ∈ V, j ∈ K to i ∈ V, a ∈ K. This repairs an indexing error in the formal loss definition by summing over the conditioning augmentation index. The assumptions, theorem, corollary, and remaining derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about biologically supervised GRN representation learning, conventional GCL as a special case, and improved performance across the downstream tasks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of biological relevance, latent-space collapse, subtype separation, and alternative-metric performance are unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitation that effectiveness was validated using teacher knockdowns from the same cancer type.

D1.justification: Appendices B–E retain the same pseudocode, data-processing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, and computation-time information. Both versions still provide the same placeholder code link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, Appendix D's positioning of GRN-estimation methods, and all 42 reference entries are unchanged. The relationship claimed between SupGCL and earlier GCL methods is also unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 corrects 'contractive learning' to 'contrastive learning,' and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The section organization and surrounding prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–12 retain the same content, captions, structure, and placement. Tiny encoding differences in embedded images do not alter the diagrams or plotted results; there is no substantive layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an inconsistent summation index in the central loss definition and Appendix A, making the mathematical expression agree with the stated node–augmentation formulation. Together with the terminology correction, this provides a limited improvement in precision. The empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
